features.heading: What you can do with SVG to Image
features.intro: Useful output choices, clear limits, and processing on your device.

items.title: Turn vector artwork into a familiar image
items.description: Paste SVG code or fetch a public SVG URL, then rasterize it into an image. Active content and external references are restricted for safer processing.

items.title: Stay in control of your source file
items.description: Processing uses this browser rather than a server-side media job. Keep the tab open, and save the result before leaving the page.

steps.heading: How to use SVG to Image
steps.intro: From your source file to a result you can save, in three steps.

items.title: Add SVG code or a URL
items.body: Paste your SVG markup, or enter a public SVG URL that allows browser access.

items.title: Choose an image format
items.body: Select PNG, JPG, or WebP and set the available output options.

items.title: Save the raster image
items.body: Save the converted file and inspect the dimensions and appearance.

items.question: Why does an SVG URL sometimes fail?
items.answer: The source may block browser access, require sign-in or return something other than SVG. If you own the file, try pasting its SVG code instead.

items.question: Is my file uploaded?
items.answer: Pasted SVG code is converted in the browser. URL input makes a request to the external site hosting the SVG, which must allow that request. The SVG is not uploaded for server-side conversion.

items.question: What if processing fails or takes too long?
items.answer: Keep this tab open and try a shorter or smaller file when possible. Available memory and media support differ between devices and browsers. Your original file is not overwritten.

items.question: Do I need AI credits to use this tool?
items.answer: No. This browser-local tool does not spend AI credits. File allowances and browser capabilities still apply.
